column2: aptus Philippines brief target 4 — Philippine restrictions (what SAP states it does not support)
EMPTY, AND THE EMPTINESS IS THE DELIVERABLE. Zero data rows. Not one sentence on the pages walked states that something is not supported in or for the Philippines.

IDENTICAL to the rule that produced the 539 rows of not-supported.tsv, deliberately, so the two files are comparable. A sentence is kept when it contains: is/are/was/were/can/could/will/would/shall/may/might/do/does/did/has/have + not + (supported|available|released|possible|permitted|allowed|covered|provided|delivered|offered); does/do not support; is/are unsupported; not supported by/for/in/with/on; no plans/support to/for; out of scope; is not part of; is/are excluded from; is/are not in scope. Conditional openings and parenthetical asides are dropped, as before.

the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 2608 PHILIPPINES localisation deliverable in full — https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_S4HANA_CLOUD/88520ff2932b479090ed3b7b116b2e91/ — 127 topics in its table of contents, 125 returned a body, 237,659 characters of text. Matches under the rule: 0 (1 sentence matched and was dropped as conditional).

the entire 12959-page corpus WS13 already harvested (55 deliverables, 40 of them country localisations), re-scanned for any sentence that both matches the rule AND names the Philippines, BIR or MyInvois. Matches: 0.

for the avoidance of doubt, the Philippines deliverable's text contains: "not support" 0 times, "unsupported" 0, "limitation" 0, "out of scope" 0, "only supported" 0, "no plans" 0, "not possible" 0, "not allowed" 0, "not available" 1, "cannot" 2, "excluded" 4, "restrict" 11. SAP writes this localisation without non-support language.

the 1 "not available", 2 "cannot" and related sentences ARE real published constraints, but they do not match the rule above. Rather than widen the rule for one country and break comparability with not-supported.tsv, they are carried verbatim in not-supported-ph-evidence.tsv beside this file. If aptus widens the rule, it must re-run Malaysia and the other 39 countries too, or the counts stop meaning the same thing.

the brief asks specifically whether SAP publishes a Philippine equivalent of Malaysia's five Peppol cross-border restrictions. It does not, and the reason is upstream of any restriction: SAP publishes NO Philippine e-invoicing capability at all at this release. The Philippines deliverable mentions "Peppol" 0 times, "electronic invoice" 0 times, "e-invoic" 0 times, and "EIS" 0 times (it mentions BIR 25 times, all in statutory-reporting contexts). SAP's own "Supported Compliance Tasks" page for SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, Cloud Edition (https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_DRC_CLOUD/2a3507bf3ad7408fa7185a757bc82ed0/1ece455e0dc6432a821c343e0e437f98.html) enumerates 35 countries across 487 task rows — Malaysia, Singapore and Vietnam among them — and the Philippines is not one of them. There is no BIR EIS restriction to record because there is no BIR EIS feature. That absence is recorded in not-supported-ph-evidence.tsv, NOT here, because absence from an enumeration is not a sentence in which SAP states a non-support, and statement_verbatim must be SAP's own sentence.

the brief names scope_item_codes and statement_verbatim. The file WS13 loaded on 07 Sep 2026 uses scope_item_ids and sap_statement_verbatim. This file follows the BRIEF's names. If the WS13 loader keys on the older names, rename these two headers — the data is unaffected.
anonymous reads of help.sap.com's own published content service. No login, no scraping, no api.sap.com traffic.
the register uses full English names; had there been rows, country would read exactly "Philippines".

floor. Anonymous help.sap.com only. SAP Notes and Knowledge Base Articles live behind authentication on me.sap.com and were NOT read — the same gap not-supported.tsv carries. A Philippine restriction published only as a KBA would not be visible to this walk.
this file does not claim SAP publishes no Philippine restriction anywhere. It states that the pages named above contain none.
